components.name: Z2 parity disjoint sets
components.cite: CP-Algorithms, Disjoint Set Union, parity and union-by-size sections; OPERATIONS.md

provenance.method: observer-only sys.settrace on original CARD-side functions; no source changes

declaration.update: The card is Z2-labeled (parity / weighted) union-find, the standard online solver for XOR-pair equations x_a ⊕ x_b = s. This is the same as online 2-coloring and bipartiteness checking, and it is the labeled union-find of W4411260212 specialized to the group Z2. Symbol by symbol: P[i] is the union-find parent pointer parent[i]. H[i] is the edge label (potential) to the parent, label[i] = x_i ⊕ x_{parent(i)}. M[r] is the size field used by union by size. Find(i) is the standard non-compressing find, returning (root, xor of labels along the path). DEMO(a,b,s) on distinct roots is the labeled union: attach root v under root u with label[v] = h_a ⊕ h_b ⊕ s. This is the textbook formula that keeps x_a ⊕ x_b = s after merging. DEMO(a,b,s) on equal roots is the standard cycle-consistency check, flagging a contradiction if h_a ⊕ h_b ≠ s. C is the usual sticky 'unsatisfiable / not bipartite' flag. The readout ASK(a,b) is the standard query: if same root and consistent, return h_a ⊕ h_b, else 'unknown'. The card encodes 'unknown' as probability 0.5, the uniform posterior under fair independent latent bits. The equations coincide line for line, including the tie-breaking rule. The 'gauge' per component is the free global flip of each connected component's 2-coloring, a standard fact about the solution set of a homogeneous-plus-offset GF(2) system on a graph. None of the listed neural forms is a meaningful match (rnn, ssm, linear_attention or hopfield). Any finite state machine is trivially an RNN, but that mapping carries no content. The correct reduction is to this known algorithm.

components.name: PGL(2,p) list-then-eliminate version space
components.cite: Mitchell 1997 chapter 6; Steif section 4.1 Theorem 4.1; OPERATIONS.md

provenance.method: observer-only sys.settrace on original CARD-side functions; no source changes

declaration.update:
The card is the candidate-elimination (version-space) algorithm, with the Bayes-optimal posterior predictive, for the hypothesis class G = PGL(2,p) acting on P^1(F_p). It is packaged as a hand-coded finite-state transducer over the token stream.

(1) Hypothesis space: H = PGL(2,p) with a uniform prior pi. H_A is the version space, meaning the hypotheses consistent with all labeled examples so far.

(2) State: (A, r) is a compressed boundary representation of the version space. Sharp 3-transitivity means the set of hypotheses consistent with r <= 3 distinct pairs is exactly the coset determined by those pairs, so storing the pairs stores H_A.

(3) Update: U(A,r,x,y) is the candidate-elimination step with an indicator likelihood 1[g(x)=y]. Its cases are:
- keep a consistent duplicate;
- collapse to the empty version space (r = -1) when a pair breaks injectivity or functionality;
- append a new constraint;
- at r = 3, test the example against the unique remaining hypothesis.

(4) Reconstruction: T_A = M(beta)^{-1} M(alpha) is the classical three-point Möbius interpolation, i.e. the cross-ratio normal form. Each frame matrix M(u1,u2,u3) sends (u1,u2,u3) to (infinity,0,1).

(5) Response readout: P_next on response tokens is the Bayes posterior predictive under the uniform prior on H_A.
- r = 3: a point mass at T_A(s).
- s anchored: a point mass at beta_i.
- s unanchored, r < 3: uniform over the V-r unused outputs, because the coset acts regularly on them.
- empty version space: uniform fallback.

(6) Free-energy equation: KL(q||pi) - E_q log 1[g in H_A] is minimized by the exact posterior. This is the standard identity that variational inference with an unrestricted q recovers Bayes' rule, so the free-energy layer adds no mechanism.

(7) Active policy: a_star is a membership query in the Angluin sense, or equivalently a query-by-committee query. Every unanchored point has equal information gain, so the policy reduces to 'query any unqueried point', with a fixed tie-break.

(8) Sequence-model form: the parser (phi, s) together with (A, r) is a finite-state machine with a fixed, non-learned transition and readout.
